correctness.rationale: Deconing the line x=0 identifies the projective complement with the affine grid-and-diagonal complement. Along the given deformation, horizontal heights are distinct; s≠0 makes the diagonal transverse to both parallel classes; and excluding each reciprocal vertical coordinate from the extra u_j's leaves exactly the specified shared-index triples. The three directions stay distinct at infinity, so the full projective lattice, not just the finite intersections, is constant. The ordered configuration space is path-connected (one can move into temporary distinct positions and then to the target, avoiding finitely many forbidden points at each move), and affords a piecewise smooth lattice isotopy. In the terminal real arrangement, b=b_q is the unique smallest horizontal height, 0<b<1/2. The open triangle y<1, z<b, y+z>1 has 1-b<y<1 and 0<z<b, so no other line cuts it. At its three vertices the only incident lines are its two sides, including when p=q=2. The simple-triangle obstruction applies, and Randell invariance transfers nonasphericity back. Correct the citation trail in any future edition: Dimca–Sticlaru Proposition 4.3 cites Falk (1995), Example 2.7, for the obstruction; it does not cite the frozen source's alternate Falk–Randell attribution there. This bibliographic issue does not affect the criterion used or the claim.
residual_risks: The original Randell full text was not accessible on the tried routes; the invariance statement was checked in the application and citation by Dimca–Sticlaru. The alternative 1987 reference was not verified. The 114 sampled cases provide no needed proof of the topological quantifier.

value.rationale: The result settles the complement topology question for a natural explicit two-parameter family that previously had only special cases in its construction paper. It shows why a complex lattice isotopy can expose a real simple-triangle obstruction not immediately visible in the given real realization, rather than giving an unmotivated parameter cutoff or repeating those special cases.
residual_risks: No general classification of near-free arrangements or determination of higher homotopy groups is claimed.
